events.text: I’ve inspected the initial scene from multiple views and flattened both feet onto the floor with all joints inside their limits. I’m moving the left hand below the nearby coat hook so it can close around the pole from a clear, non-overlapping position. The controller will use SONIC for body motion and joint-level grasp and arm corrections.

events.text: The failed trial exposed two issues: the first palm target was near the arm’s reach limit, and the closing fingers did not capture the pole. I’m moving the initial stance closer and fitting a three-finger grasp with small positive surface gaps, checking that the grasp starts without overlap.

events.text: The two-hand initial state now passes the checks: no active penetrations, no joint-limit violations, and the object pose and zero velocity are unchanged. I’ve also inspected the rendered posture. The next rollout will test whether this grasp holds through the full translation and rotation.

events.text: A firmer single-hand grip performed much better: mean ADD is 0.096 m, position error 0.074 m, and orientation error 11.6°. It maintained a continuous lift for about 3.1 seconds, with the robot upright throughout. I’m checking the endpoint and testing small feedback corrections to reduce the remaining tracking error.

events.text: The latest rollout completes the carry and sets the stand down without a fall or drop. Mean errors are 0.063 m ADD, 0.040 m position, and 7.70° orientation. The hand loses contact around 10 seconds, and the stand remains independently supported through the 14-second finish. I’m running the final reproducibility check and saving the submission.
